fine_trace.note: Client banner 'SSH-2.0-poc' parsed; connection callback switches socket data callback to ssh_packet_socket_callback.
Plaintext SSH packet (type 50) received and buffered; packet_state INIT, no crypto active.
Dispatcher routes SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST (50) to ssh_packet_userauth_request regardless of session state.
First unpack 'sss' succeeds (user/service/password); method=="password" triggers second unpack with mixed format "bs".

fine_trace.code: case 'b': o.byte = va_arg(ap, uint8_t *); rlen = ssh_buffer_get_u8(buffer, o.byte); rc = rlen==1 ? SSH_OK : SSH_ERROR; ... case 's': o.cstring = va_arg(ap, char **); *o.cstring = NULL; rc = ssh_buffer_get_u32(buffer, &u32len); if (rc != 4){ rc = SSH_ERROR; break; }
fine_trace.note: 'b' consumes the non-zero boolean byte (OK); 's' has no 4-byte length left so get_u32 returns 0 and rc becomes SSH_ERROR.

fine_trace.code: case 'b': if (buffer->secure) { o.byte = va_arg(ap_copy, uint8_t *); ... } break; ... case 's': o.cstring = va_arg(ap_copy, char **); if (buffer->secure) { ... } SAFE_FREE(*o.cstring);
fine_trace.note: Rollback: buffer not secure so 'b' does not consume va_arg from ap_copy; 's' then reads the uint8_t* argument as char**, and SAFE_FREE(*o.cstring) frees the attacker-controlled boolean value (0x01) -> invalid free -> crash in ssh_buffer_unpack.

vuln_logic: In ssh_buffer_unpack_va (src/buffer.c) the error-rollback loop only consumes va_list arguments for numeric formats ('b','w','d','q') when buffer->secure is set. On a non-secure buffer (all network packet buffers), a failed unpack whose format mixes a numeric specifier with 's'/'S' misaligns ap_copy: the 's' rollback then dereferences the wrong argument and SAFE_FREE()s an attacker-controlled pointer (the boolean byte 0x01), causing an invalid free / invalid memory access inside ssh_buffer_unpack.
